PullRequest.Title: Add transient UI for /btw side questions
PullRequest.Body:

`/btw` is intended for a lightweight tangent, but today it opens another full chat. This change keeps the source transcript and composer in place and renders the side answer in a transient card directly above the existing composer.

## Reviewer TL;DR

The core design is **a normal durable side chat with a transient presentation**:

- The provider still creates and owns a real side chat with its own resource, model, request/response state, history, and recovery path.
- Sessions stores only resource identities for the transient card and resolves current provider facades reactively.
- Closing removes only the card; the backing chat remains in Closed chats.
- **Open Full Chat** opens that same chat through the normal `ISessionsService.openChat` path.
- If the treatment is disabled, the source cannot host a card, or the source becomes read-only, orchestration uses/remains with the normal full side-chat surface.
- The feature is default-off behind `chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` (`config.chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` in ExP).

**Invariant:** `/btw` changes only how the side chat is presented. It does not hide, replace, move, rebind, or restyle the source composer.

## Suggested review order

| Commit | Purpose | Main review question |
|---|---|---|
| `0ad5cdda4f3` `chat: refactor: support embedded response widgets` | Generic response-only widget options, hidden-input layout, and focus-local embedded action routing | Do defaults preserve every existing full-chat caller? |
| `7ae3696a8e3` `sessions: refactor: make send lifecycle explicit` | Request-ID correlation, `preserveActiveChat`, close history, and a fail-closed provider option boundary | Can overlapping/failing sends affect the wrong navigation follow or leak UI-only options? |
| `1e0803878d6` `sessions: feat: add transient side-chat presentation` | Complete experiment gate, card, orchestration, all entry points, accessibility, failure handling, and tests | Can any race leave stale state, leaked models, duplicate errors, or a hidden/headless chat? |
| `6a4fe0a2a16` `agentHost: polish: skip side-chat rename round-trip` | Independent latency optimization | Is rename guidance suppressed only for `SideChat` origins? |

The durable contract is documented in `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md` under **Transient side questions**.

## Flow

```text
/btw, response-selection Ask Question, or workbench Ask in Side Chat
  -> create a real provider-backed side chat
  -> ISideChatOrchestrationService.prepare(...)
     -> control / no live interactive source host: open + split full side chat
     -> treatment + live source host: close with skipHistory + publish transient state
  -> prepared.send(...)
     -> transient: awaited send with preserveActiveChat
     -> full: normal foreground send
  -> provider streams into the side-chat model
  -> source ChatView renders the response-only card
```

`show()` revalidates the rollout setting, host, session, source chat, side chat, source interactivity, and a per-source monotonic presentation ID after its awaited close. Overlapping questions cannot overwrite each other. Disabling the setting, disposing the final host, deleting either chat, replacing/removing the provider facade, or making the source read-only removes live transient state.

A full-chat fallback is verified active before sending, so a side chat cannot become hidden and headless.

## Latest-main layout integration

Latest `main` floats `.chat-input-persistent-content` in a fixed-height, pointer-events-controlled lane for status pills. A growing interactive card cannot use that lane.

The card is therefore an in-flow child of `ChatInputPart.element`, after the floating pills container and before banners and the unchanged composer:

```text
ChatInputPart
├── floating persistent-content lane (status pills)
├── transient side-question card (in flow)
├── banners
└── original composer
```

`SessionChatInputToolbar.onDidChangeVisibility` remains the authoritative owner-driven signal for hidden-input persistent content. This avoids both `:has()` and the self-latching mistake of measuring a descendant after its ancestor becomes `display: none`.

## Embedded response renderer

The card reuses `ChatWidget` so Markdown, code blocks, tools, subagents, confirmations, errors, accessibility, and workbench scrolling stay consistent. It is configured with:

- response rows only;
- no response header/footer, follow-ups, pet, or scroll-to-bottom button;
- a hidden input;
- deterministic completed-work disclosure;
- `isEmbedded: true`.

Embedded widgets become `lastFocusedWidget` only while their DOM has focus, so keyboard actions target the side model. They are excluded from global widget enumeration, resource/input lookup, focus/visibility events, and background-session notifications. `lastFocusedChatSurface` remains stable for voice, mode synchronization, MCP UI, extension-host state, and other consumers that intentionally follow full chat surfaces.

The nested widget/model/listeners are created lazily and disposed with the card. Loads are cancellation- and identity-guarded. Streaming layout is animation-frame coalesced, unchanged dimensions are skipped, activity plaintext is memoized, and label DOM writes are equality-guarded.

Short answers stay compact. Long answers grow until the outer card reaches 60% of the source view, then scroll inside the existing workbench list while remaining anchored at the start.

## Failure, focus, and accessibility

`ChatSideChatSendResultKind.FailedAndPresented` identifies failures already owned by a live card. Transient failures render once in the card; if the card was dismissed first, the original error rejects to the caller for normal notification/restoration. Full-chat failures always reject normally.

The card is a labelled region described by its question and visible status. Announcements are transition-based for creation, replacement, completion, failure, and `NeedsInput`.

Escape uses scoped keybindings:

- from the card, it dismisses even while the answer streams;
- code-editor selections, suggestion UI, and editor hover keep precedence;
- from the source input, active requests, dictation, editing, confirmations, elicitations, and question carousels also keep precedence.

Close restores source-composer focus. Promotion verifies and focuses the full-chat destination.

## Testing

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- every intermediate commit type-checked independently
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- ESLint across all 61 changed TypeScript files
- Stylelint across all changed CSS
- Sessions suite: **3,038 passing**
- Workbench Chat suite: **6,539 passing**
- Agent Host title suite: **44 passing**
- Four independent Opus 5 max-reasoning reviews covering architecture/layering, correctness/races, performance/lifecycle, and regressions/tests; all high-confidence findings were addressed and re-reviewed
- Live authenticated Agents-window verification of:
  - provider-backed progress and completion;
  - one unchanged source composer and no request row inside the card;
  - in-flow placement outside the floating pills lane;
  - source draft preservation and refocus on close;
  - Escape dismissal during streaming;
  - verified **Open Full Chat** promotion;
  - disabled-setting full-chat split fallback;
  - long-answer cap and internal scrolling (526px card in a 949px window; 1,619px scroll extent in a 469px response viewport).

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every active-agent side-chat turn could read title metadata and inject guidance forcing an unnecessary rename_chat tool invocation.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Side-chat sends paid avoidable metadata I/O and rename-tool latency before completing the side answer.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Side-chat turns now exit title preparation before the metadata read and rename_chat guidance, removing that repeated work from the answer path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: SessionTitleContribution.onOutgoingTurn awaits prepareInstructionForAgent on every outgoing turn. In the base revision, line 523 awaited _readPersistedTitleMetadata, which opens the session database and reads metadata; for an automatic title the method then returned an instruction that explicitly requires rename_chat. The new SideChat-origin guard returns before both operations, and the added test verifies this path returns undefined for a side chat.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ask a /btw or selection-based side question with transient presentation enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider-backed side-chat creation must complete, then transient show closes the side chat locally and the awaited provider send must settle. The embedded model acquisition starts after publication but is not awaited by send orchestration; it is required for the card to render the streamed answer rather than to dispatch the request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the provider side chat and send one request through ISessionsManagementService/ISessionsProvider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create and one send per side question; no per-response-part provider fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same side-chat create and send operations occurred before the diff, with a full-chat open between them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both provider operations are on the side-question completion path; creation precedes send and send is awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire an existing chat model or resolve the remote side-chat session once for the embedded renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquisition per presented side-chat resource per live host; an existing model reference is reused on a warm cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The normal full-chat surface loaded the same backing side-chat model as part of opening/rendering the side chat; there was no embedded-card path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by request dispatch, but card rendering waits for it; it can overlap the provider send.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active transient state per source chat, after replacement coalescing; multiplicity is bounded by live source hosts, while response rendering scales with streamed response parts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Create is serialized before presentation and send. Cold embedded model acquisition may overlap the single provider send; animation-frame scheduling coalesces content-height relayouts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm model acquisition reuses ChatService's existing session model. Cold acquisition resolves the remote session once. Transient state is not a data cache and replacement drops the old model reference.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the create/show/send sequence, non-awaited model acquisition, reference disposal, and RAF coalescing are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote provider/model latency varies, and duplicate live hosts for one source are expected to be uncommon.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: expensive provider cardinality is unchanged, model loading replaces the prior full-chat model load and is moved off the send-dispatch critical path, and streaming layout is coalesced with unchanged dimensions skipped.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ask a side question when the experiment is disabled or no live source host is available
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider side-chat creation, full-chat activation/session loading, optional split placement, and provider send remain serialized before the user receives the answer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the side chat, resolve/open its normal chat surface, and send through the provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create, one open/session resolution, and one send per side question.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, every side question followed create, open/split, then send. The diff adds only the transient eligibility check before taking this same fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Open is verified before the send, matching the prior foreground side-chat workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation sequence per explicit side-question action; no collection fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The create/open/send sequence is serialized; no new burst or parallel provider calls are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The transient service immediately returns on the default-off configuration. Normal session/model caches apply to openChat as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: fallback control flow and tests establish identical provider-call cardinality and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and session-open latency depend on backend and cache state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the default-off path preserves the old expensive boundary sequence and adds only bounded in-process eligibility work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream, resize, dismiss, replace, or promote a transient side-question card
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Streaming model events update the embedded transcript. Card height work is deferred to at most one animation-frame callback; promotion awaits the normal openChat path, while dismissal/replacement synchronously releases listeners, widget, and model references.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the same backing side chat through SessionsService when the user selects Open Full Chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one open attempt per promotion action; repeated clicks are disabled while promoting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before transient presentation, the backing side chat was already opened as the normal surface, so no later promotion action existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The promotion UI waits for chat activation verification.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Response content and source-view dimensions control renderer/layout cost; one state replaces another per source, and historical announcement maps are pruned when states disappear.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Streaming relayout requests are coalesced to one per animation frame. Promotion is guarded by a promoting flag and replacement uses monotonic presentation IDs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Promotion normally reuses the model reference already acquired by the card. Dismissal clears the reference rather than retaining a hidden renderer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: model/listener ownership, cancellation, RAF coalescing, equality guards, and promotion serialization are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Response complexity and stream rate vary, but layout frequency and retained-state cardinality are explicitly bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the full embedded widget is lazy, dimensions are guarded, and cancellation/disposal paths release model, DOM, listeners, and scheduled work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send normal foreground or preserved side-chat requests while other sends overlap
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each foreground request fires a correlated will/end lifecycle around the existing provider send. Preserved transient sends skip active-chat following but remain awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the provider sendRequest once with management-only options removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one provider send per request; lifecycle events do not add provider calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider send already occurred once per request. The diff changes follow ownership and cleanup correlation, not boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider completion remains the awaited critical path; request-ID event correlation adds synchronous in-process notifications only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with explicit concurrent sends, not session/chat collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Overlapping sends retain independent request IDs; only the newest foreground follow is active, and a preserved send does not clear it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Telemetry prewarming behavior remains event-driven; no new cache or invalidation path is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: request IDs and preserveActiveChat guards are explicit and covered by overlap/failure tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual provider concurrency is backend-controlled, but this diff does not add sends or increase their parallelism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added lifecycle signaling is constant work per send and fixes cleanup ownership without increasing provider traffic.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send an active-agent turn in a provider-backed side chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Outgoing-turn contributions run before the agent send. The new SideChat-origin guard exits title preparation before session-metadata I/O or automatic rename guidance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the session database and read title-source metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously up to one metadata read per eligible outgoing side-chat turn; now zero for SideChat origins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Eligible side-chat turns awaited the metadata read and could inject mandatory rename_chat guidance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The awaited metadata read is removed from side-chat outgoing-turn preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Automatic title guidance could force a rename_chat tool loop during the agent turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously up to one rename instruction/tool invocation per eligible side-chat turn until title state changed; now zero for SideChat origins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Side chats inherited the same automatic rename reminder as normal independent chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The change removes avoidable tool work from side-answer latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Savings scale with eligible side-chat turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrency is added; the previously awaited work is removed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new origin check is in-memory and bypasses persisted metadata regardless of database cache warmth.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the performance fix was recorded against the blamed introducing commit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tool-loop duration depends on agent/provider behavior, but the mandatory guidance and database boundary are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes a concrete repeated-work latency regression; it is not a review finding against the fixing change.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 65 changed files and the full new transient widget/service implementations. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold. The transient path preserves provider-call cardinality, keeps model loading off request dispatch, coalesces streaming layout, and disposes retained resources. Recorded the side-chat title guard as a regression fix because it removes per-turn metadata I/O and automatic rename-tool work.
